findings.reason: §1's premise that "reckon writes that bucket" is false as written and would be corrected so the plan's own account of today's behaviour matches §3's.
findings.text: §1 states "At promotion, `reckon/crew/reports.py` (near line 2797) turns each entry into a plan followup", but §3 (plan.html:58) states the same function `followup_ops_from_manifest` "has no production caller" and is deleted; `grep -rn followup_ops_from_manifest reckon scripts` returns only its definition (`reckon/crew/reports.py:2790`) and its export name (`reckon/crew.py:193`), with no call on any production path, so promotion does not perform the conversion §1 attributes to it and the two sections contradict each other about the current mechanism

findings.reason: §3 must add `reckon/ledger.py` to its write paths (or §6 must be told to update that docstring), otherwise a source occurrence the plan intends to purge is left behind and unreachable by the node that renames the field.
findings.text: §3 renames the manifest field `follow_ons` and lists its write paths, but omits `reckon/ledger.py`: `reckon/ledger.py:651`'s docstring ("Extract the repository paths a manifest's ``follow_ons`` name") carries that same field name, and §6 — the section whose write paths do include `reckon/ledger.py` — explicitly keeps the field's old name ("The manifest field keeps its old name here"), so after §3 lands the retired word survives in that docstring with no write path covering it

response_events.reason: §1 is the landed census section; §3 records the mechanism as it stands, a conversion function with no production caller applied by coordinators through two skill references, and the build follows §3
